extraction.document_summary: AIA Platinum International Health is a worldwide (excluding USA) international medical insurance plan with lifetime global medical coverage and high overall limits. The brochure states maximum claim limits of S$750,000 per policy year and S$5,000,000 per lifetime for Plan 1, versus S$1,500,000 per policy year and S$10,000,000 per lifetime for Plan 2, with “Maximum coverage period: Lifetime.” Reimbursement is generally “as charged” for many hospital items, but the plan requires choosing one deductible/co-insurance option: Option 1 (deductible S$1,500; co-insurance 10%, capped at S$15,000 per policy year) or Option 2 (deductible S$3,000; co-insurance 15%, capped at S$20,000 per policy year). It covers hospital, pre- (up to 90 days) and post-hospitalisation (up to 90 days), outpatient day surgery, emergency accidental outpatient treatment (within 24 hours of accident, up to 30 days), plus capped benefits for items such as outpatient dialysis (S$300,000/year) and proton beam therapy (S$100,000/year). Key caveats stated include exclusions for pre-existing conditions and an illness waiting period of at least 30 days.
quality_notes: Product name, territorial scope, lifetime limit, and core benefit caps are clearly stated in tables.
Deductible/co-insurance options (Option 1/Option 2) are stated, but the document does not explicitly link which deductible option must be paired with Plan 1 vs Plan 2.
Some benefits are listed as 'as charged' and caps are provided for certain therapies/treatments; the brochure does not state a universal claims methodology beyond deductible/co-insurance.
Important underwriting/eligibility details (e.g., entry age, renewal, medical underwriting type) are not provided.

policies.quick_summary: Worldwide (excluding USA) lifetime medical coverage with high annual and lifetime claim limits. Pays “as charged” for many hospital/outpatient expenses subject to selected deductible/co-insurance (Option 1 or Option 2). Covers pre- and post-hospitalisation treatment (up to 90 days before/after), outpatient day surgery, emergency accidental outpatient treatment (within 24 hours; up to 30 days), and capped special treatments such as outpatient kidney dialysis (S$300,000/year) and proton beam therapy (S$100,000/year). Brochure states exclusions for pre-existing conditions and an illness waiting period of at least 30 days.
important_caveats: Brochure states there are exclusions such as pre-existing conditions where no benefits will be payable.
Brochure states there is a waiting period of at least 30 days for illness.
Teladoc Health Personal Case Management service is stated as not a contractual benefit and subject to Teladoc terms.
